content.text: {"primary_meaning":"In mainstream Christian teaching, bread primarily symbolizes Jesus Christ himself as the source of spiritual life and divine sustenance — the 'Bread of Life' — a meaning concentrated in and reinforced by the Eucharist/Lord's Supper, where bread represents (or, in sacramental traditions, becomes) Christ's body given for believers. Behind this stands the broader biblical motif of bread as God's life-giving provision, typified by the manna in the wilderness, which Christian interpreters read as foreshadowing Christ.","primary_basis":["John 6:35 ('I am the bread of life')","John 6:48-58 (bread from heaven; living bread; eating his flesh)","Matthew 26:26 / Mark 14:22 / Luke 22:19 ('This is my body' at the Last Supper)","1 Corinthians 11:23-26 (institution of the Lord's Supper)","Exodus 16 (manna as God's provision, read typologically of Christ)","John 6:31-33 (manna contrasted with the true bread from heaven)","Luke 24:30-35 (Christ known in the breaking of bread)","Matthew 14:13-21 and parallels (feeding of the five thousand as sign leading into the Bread of Life discourse)"],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Bread as the Word of God / spiritual nourishment from Scripture — humans live 'not by bread alone but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God.'","basis":["Deuteronomy 8:3","Matthew 4:4 / Luke 4:4","Amos 8:11 (famine of hearing the words of the LORD)","Isaiah 55:1-3"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Bread as God's daily physical provision and dependence on God for material needs, especially in the petition for 'daily bread.'","basis":["Matthew 6:11 / Luke 11:3 (Lord's Prayer)","Genesis 3:19 (bread by the sweat of the brow)","Psalm 104:14-15","Proverbs 30:8"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Bread as fellowship, communion, and the unity of the church — one loaf signifying one body of believers, expressed in shared table fellowship.","basis":["1 Corinthians 10:16-17","Acts 2:42, 46 (breaking of bread)","Acts 20:7"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Unleavened bread as purity, sincerity, and freedom from sin (with leaven as corruption), tied to Passover typology.","basis":["Exodus 12:8, 15-20","1 Corinthians 5:6-8","Matthew 16:6, 11-12 (leaven of the Pharisees)"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The bread of the Presence (showbread) in the tabernacle/temple as symbol of covenant fellowship with God and, typologically, of Christ's abiding presence.","basis":["Exodus 25:30","Leviticus 24:5-9","1 Samuel 21:1-6 with Matthew 12:3-4","Hebrews 9:2"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Bread as suffering, hardship, or affliction ('bread of affliction,' 'bread of tears,' 'bread of adversity').","basis":["Deuteronomy 16:3","Psalm 80:5","Psalm 127:2","Isaiah 30:20"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Bread as anticipation of the eschatological messianic banquet — eating bread in the kingdom of God.","basis":["Luke 14:15","Isaiah 25:6","Matthew 8:11","Luke 22:16-18, 30"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Bread as hospitality and covenant/peace between persons, such that sharing bread creates a bond (and betrayal by a table companion is aggravated treachery).","basis":["Genesis 18:5-6","Psalm 41:9","John 13:18","Genesis 14:18 (Melchizedek bringing bread and wine)"],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"Bread is among the most stable and heavily attested symbols in Christian interpretation. The dominant reading — Christ as the Bread of Life and the eucharistic body of Christ — is shared across Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant traditions, though traditions differ sharply on the mode (transubstantiation, real presence, memorial symbol); that dispute concerns the mechanics of the sacrament, not the symbolic referent. The alternative readings listed are not rival identifications so much as complementary layers of a rich, multivalent symbol; most commentators treat several of them together, with the Word-of-God and daily-provision senses often folded into the christological reading (e.g., patristic and Reformation exegesis of 'daily bread' as both material need and Christ/the Word)."}
